sources: SEC investor education and FINRA referenced

competitors.gaps: Does not combine metrics, such as beta with drawdown, or cover valuation and balance-sheet risk.

sources: S&P 500 as benchmark; no specific studies cited

competitors.gaps: No drawdown, Sharpe ratio, leverage, or valuation risk.

competitors.title: Standard Deviation, Beta, Alpha, and Sharpe Ratio Explained for Advisors
headings: Standard Deviation: What Volatility Actually Measures
coverage: R-squared as a check on beta
sources: Academic citations including Evans and Archer (1968) and Fama and French (1992)
NYU Stern industry betas and SPIVA
link_patterns: Internal links to related adviser content

competitors.gaps: Centered on volatility; little on drawdown, leverage, or valuation-based risk.

competitors.title: 5 Overlooked Metrics That Smart Investors Use to Find Long-Term Winning Stocks
sources: Alphabet financials from the publisher's own platform
data_assets: Historical margin, cash flow, and ROIC charts
competitors.covered_well: Explains five quality metrics with one worked company example.
competitors.gaps: Covers business quality, not risk: no beta, volatility, drawdown, or leverage ratios.

competitors.title: Maximum Drawdown (MDD) | Formula + Calculator
competitors.covered_well: Walks through the peak-to-trough calculation with a transparent example.
competitors.gaps: Treats drawdown alone; no link to beta, leverage, or recovery time.

content_gaps: The primary keyword returns scattered results with no single clear guide.
Explainers found for related searches cover beta and standard deviation but stop at volatility.
Drawdown, leverage, and valuation risk are treated on separate pages, if at all.
Few pages show how the metrics disagree with each other.
value_add: One page that reads the main risk metrics together, shows drawdown and recovery arithmetic, and says what each number leaves out.
